programs.title: Iron Curtain: Life Under Soviet Occupation
programs.desc:
A story about the Sovietization process, from 1944 to the construction of the Berlin Wall.After World War II, the countries of Central and Eastern Europe found themselves in the Soviet zone.The events that led to such a division of the Old Continent will be presented.Viewers will learn how it affected the everyday lives of citizens of these countries and what forms of resistance they encountered.Experts will explain the mechanisms of Soviet domination.There will be witnesses' accounts, interviews, discussions of scientific works and archives including propaganda films, home recordings and fictional stories.
After Stalin's death, it became possible to introduce reforms in the USSR.Protests broke out in Czechoslovakia and Bulgaria, and the strike in the GDR turned into a national uprising.On the night of February 24-25, 1956, Nikita Khrushchev delivered a secret report during the 20th Congress of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union, in which he condemned the criminal system created by his predecessor.In October, there was a revolt in Poland, and a month later Soviet tanks crushed the Hungarian uprising.Five years later, the Berlin Wall, a symbol of the division of Europe, was built.
